Citizenship is both legal membership and active participation. The course materials frame citizens as people who can help shape government and society, not just people who possess a passport. Citizens participate by voting, joining parties, protesting, volunteering, following laws, challenging unjust laws, and organizing with others around common concerns.

Civil disobedience is a deliberate, public challenge to a law or policy considered unjust. It connects to citizenship because a citizen may decide that obeying the law is normally important, but that democratic responsibility can also require dissent when law violates rights or dignity.

Collectivism emphasizes shared goals, common concerns, group identity, and responsibility to others. The unit introduction asks students to consider the advantages and pitfalls of supporting a collective ideology, which means collectivism can motivate cooperation but can also pressure individuals to conform.

vocabulary.term: First Past the Post and proportional representation
vocabulary.definition: Electoral systems shape how citizens see their political voice. First Past the Post can create local representation and clear winners, but it can also leave parties with less seat share than their vote share suggests. Proportional representation tries to make seats reflect votes more closely, which can make more citizens feel represented.
aliases: First Past the Post and proportional representation

vocabulary.definition: Ideology is more than a political label. In this unit it means the beliefs and values that guide how people think society should be organized, what government should do, and what responsibilities citizens have. The unit materials connect ideology to worldview: what people experience and value can shape the ideology they are willing to support.

Individualism emphasizes personal freedom, conscience, self-reliance, and the right to make choices without unnecessary collective pressure. In this unit, it helps explain why a citizen might act from personal ideals even when a group, government, or majority expects conformity.
